Surah 82, verses 1–5

It is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1–5} That is: when the sky is split open and cracked apart, when its stars are scattered and its beauty departs, when the seas are set ablaze (fujjirat) and become one sea, and when the graves are overturned (bu'thirat), so that what is in them of the dead is brought out and they are gathered to the place of standing before Allah for recompense for their deeds. Then the veil will be lifted, what was hidden will be revealed, and every soul will know what it has brought with it of gains and losses. At that time the wrongdoer will bite his hands in regret when he sees what his hands have sent forward, and he will be certain of everlasting misery and endless punishment. And at that time the God-fearing, who sent ahead righteous deeds, will attain the great triumph, the lasting bliss, and safety from the torment of the Blazing Fire.

{6–8} Allah, exalted is He, says, rebuking the human being who falls short in his duty to Him and dares to disobey Him: ﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Most Generous?﴾ Is it out of negligence on your part regarding His rights? Or contempt on your part for His punishment? Or a lack of faith on your part in His recompense? Did He not create you and proportion you ﴿and made you balanced﴾: in the best form, and He assembled you in a upright, balanced composition, in the finest shapes and most beautiful forms? Is it fitting for you to deny the blessing of the Benefactor or to reject the kindness of the Benevolent? This is only from your ignorance, your wrongdoing, your obstinacy and your folly. So praise Allah that He did not make your form the form of a dog, a donkey, or other such animals. For this reason, Allah said: ﴿In whatever form He willed, He assembled you.﴾

{9–12} And His saying: ﴿No! Rather, you deny the Recompense.﴾ That is: despite this admonition and reminder, you continue persistently in denying the recompense, while you will surely be held to account for what you did. Allah has appointed over you noble angels who record your words and deeds and know them. This includes both the actions of the hearts and the actions of the limbs. Therefore, it is fitting for you to honor them and show them reverence.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 82, verses 13–19:

{13–19} By "the righteous" (al-abrar) is meant those who uphold the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants, and who are constant in righteousness in the deeds of the heart and the deeds of the limbs. For them the reward is bliss in the heart, the spirit and the body, in the abode of this world, in the abode of the barzakh (the intermediate state), and in the abode of permanence. ﴿And indeed the wicked (al-fujjar)﴾: those who fell short in the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants, whose hearts became corrupt so that their deeds became corrupt too. ﴿Indeed they will be in the Blazing Fire (jahim)﴾; that is, in painful punishment in the abode of this world, in the abode of the barzakh, and in the abode of permanence. ﴿They will burn in it﴾: they will be punished by it with the most severe punishment ﴿on the Day of Recompense﴾; that is, the Day of Reckoning for deeds. ﴿And they will not be absent from it﴾; that is, rather, they will be constantly in it and will not come out of it. ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is? Then what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾ In this there is a magnification of that terrible Day, which bewilders minds. ﴿The Day when no soul will have power to do anything for another soul﴾: even if that soul were a close relative or a sincere beloved; for every person is preoccupied with himself and seeks no release for anyone else. ﴿And the Command on that Day belongs to Allah﴾: He is the One who judges between the servants and takes for the oppressed his right from his oppressor. And Allah knows best.
